title: Playing Dolly in Mamba's Daughters with Ethel Waters
summary: In the 1939 Broadway show she played Dolly opposite Willie Bryant, the first Black company at the Empire.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: And then in -- in the mid-'50's, '54, '55 you were in Miss Patterson --
No, I didn't understudy Eartha Kitt. Now, well, you've got Mamba's Daughters in there already, haven't you?
No, we have to get to Mamba's Daughters.
Oh, who was in that show with you?
Ethel Waters. She starred in the show.
You were in (inaudible) the original show.
Uh-huh, Ethel Waters -- yeah, Empire -- first Negro group to ever play the Empire, 40th and Broadway.
And what did you play, what part?
In Mamba's Daughters I was Dolly. Willie Bryant -- you know -- remember Willie Bryant?

Willie Bryant was supposed to be my sweetheart in the show, and, oh, man, oh, man, I used to beat him up something terrible in the show. What was his name? It's a shame. You know, I had to act real, you know, so I used to whip that old man.
